verdicts.evidence: The `has` is a live guard, not a redundant one: readRules accepts any token matching `/^ASI\d{2}$/` from a rule's `asi:` front matter, while asiCoverage is seeded only with the ten keys of ASI_LABELS (ASI01–ASI10), and readRules reads the MISSION's own `runward/rules/` when present — operator-editable by design. RECIPE: `runward init --yes`, add `runward/rules/zz-custom.md` with front matter `asi: [ASI11]`, run `runward compliance iso-42001`. Shipped build: exit 0, `ASI coverage 10/10 categories mapped to a rule`, pack written. Mutated: `asiCoverage.get("ASI11")` is undefined, the command aborts with `✗ Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')`, exit 1, and `runward/compliance/` is never created — no readiness draft, no OSCAL.

verdicts.evidence: SENSITIVITY CONTROL: this object literal is built at the call site, handed to artifactState, and discarded. artifactState and inProgressCause (src/lib/mission.ts) read `relPath` and `templateKey` and never `label`. The control that shows the probe is sensitive: mutate `relPath` on the very same literal instead and the state flips (`filled` → `missing`) on every mission and in both surfaces. `Artifact.label` IS printed — but by `check`, from the PHASES table, never from this literal, which never escapes the call. Measured byte-identical across nine probe missions and all four documents.
